Sukhveer And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 13
February, 2024

Author: Ashwani Kumar Mishra
Bench: Ashwani Kumar Mishra
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Petitioner :- Sukhveer And Another
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Ravi Prakash Pandey
Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi,J.
1. Heard counsel for the petitioner, learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and Sri
M.N. Singh, counsel for the respondent.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2.  This petition has been filed challenging a report contained in Annexure-1 to the writ petition in respect of objections submitted by the tenure holders upon the detailed project report (DPR)
submitted by the respondents.

The second prayer made in the writ petition is to command the respondents to pay appropriate compensation in respect of Khasra Nos. 4359, 4365, 4097, 4095,
Sukhveer And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36528062/
1 4100 and Khasra/Plot Nos. 4321, 4332 and 4250 situated in Village Dasna, Tehsil and District Ghaziabad.
3.

entities.text: Sukhveer And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears that a High Teck Township is proposed to be developed at District Ghaziabad pursuant to a Government Order dated 7.4.2021.
A committee has been constituted to consider objections submitted in respect of the detailed project report in respect of such township.

This Committee has submitted its report rejecting all the objections after noticing that the objections were in respect of rate of compensation payable to the tenure holders and that none of the objections was in respect of detailed project report/layout plan.
This report has been forwarded to the State Government and it is only the State Government which has to take a final decision in respect of approval of the layout plan.

So far as the challenge to this report on the objections to the detailed project report (DPR) is concerned, we do not find any occasion to entertain writ petition, inasmuch as this report is merely a fact finding report and an ultimate decision on the DPR is awaited at the level of the State Government.
It is, otherwise, undisputed that all objections of the petitioners were in respect of the amount of compensation and did not relate to the detailed project report/layout plan.
4. In that view of the matter, we decline to grant the first relief prayed for in the writ petition.

So far as the matter of payment of compensation is concerned, the respondents have filed counter affidavit detailing the situation in respect of the plots regarding which relief is claimed by the petitioners.

Paragraph 15 and 16 of the counter affidavit are re-produced hereinunder:
"15.

That serial nos. 298, 299 & 463 of award which was declared under section 11(2)
of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
On 30.10.2012, it clearly shows that father of petitioner no.1 has already taken compensation for plot nos. 4095, 4097 and 4100 under the Karar Niyamwali, 1997.
Copy of Award is being filed herewith and marked as Annexure no. CA-3 to this affidavit.
16. That further plot nos. 4359, 4365 (petitioner no. 1) and plot nos. 4321, 4332 and 4250 (petitioner no. 2) have not been subjected to acquisition proceedings.
The same formed part of the original DPR of M/s Sun City High Tech Infrastructure Private Limited as was approved for an area of 4312.99 acres.

entities.text: Sun City High Tech Infrastructure Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
However, the same were excluded in the proposed amended DPR."
5.
In reply to the aforesaid counter affidavit, in paragraph 7 of the rejoinder affidavit, the petitioners state that they are entitled to compensation as per the new Act.
6. That is an issue which can be examined in an appropriate proceedings and no observations are required to be made in that regard.
Neither the award is annexed nor the factum of acceptance of compensation in that regard is disputed.

7. From the above assertion made in the counter affidavit, it is clear that out of eight plots in respect of which relief has been sought, five of them, as specified in the affidavit of the respondent, are not being acquired at this stage.

Petitioners, therefore, would be entitled to utilize such land in Sukhveer And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36528062/
2 accordance with law.

entities.text: Sukhveer And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as the remaining three plots are concerned, it is shown that an award under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has already been made and the compensation amount has been paid to the tenure holders.
Any dispute in respect of compensation of acquired land can always be pursued in the manner stipulated in law.
No further relief in respect of the second prayer can, thus, be granted, either.
8. The petitioners have also expressed their apprehension that they would not be able to utilize their land.

We find such apprehension to be totally misconceived, inasmuch as the law allows development within the development area of the authority in accordance with U.P. Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973.

entities.text: U.P. Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioners, therefore, cannot be permitted to raise a valid grievance that putting the tenure holders to use of land in terms of the plan would cause prejudice to them.
Argument advanced in that regard is rejected.
9. In view of the above observations, writ petition is consigned to record.
